title: Examination of School Adaptation among Preschool Children with Special Needs
text_snippet: Examination of School Adaptation among Preschool Children with Special Needs The aim of the study is to examine the school adaptation status of children with special needs receiving preschool education. The research was designed with mixed method and simultaneous design. The study group of the research consists of children with special needs who receive education in official independent kindergartens affiliated to the Ministry of National Education, special education kindergartens and schools/classrooms affiliated to the Ministry of National Education in Istanbul. The data were collected using the "Demographic Information Form", "School Adaptation Teacher Rating Scale-Short Form (OSAS-SF)" and "Semi-structured Teacher Interview Form". As a result of the study, the data obtained from the scale were analysed using the statistical program for social sciences, while the qualitative data were analysed using Maxqda 2022 qualitative data analysis program. title: Offloading cognition to artificial intelligence: A qualitative study of teachers' experiences and perceptions
text_snippet: Offloading cognition to artificial intelligence: A qualitative study of teachers' experiences and perceptions This study investigates the role of artificial intelligence (AI) assistants in teachers' cognitive and metacognitive processes through the lens of cognitive offloading theory. Adopting a phenomenological research design, the study explores how, why, and with what consequences teachers delegate mental tasks to AI. Data were collected through semi-structured online interviews with 17 teachers from various disciplines and analyzed using thematic analysis. Findings reveal that participating teachers regularly use AI assistants for both professional tasks, such as lesson planning, material design, exam preparation, and daily life activities, including information seeking and content creation. Participants perceived AI tools as reducing mental effort and time pressure and increasing their sense of self-efficacy, while their views regarding the effects of AI use on creativity were mixed. However, participatingteachers also demonstrated awareness of the risks associated with over-reliance on AI, particularly its potential to weaken critical thinking and self-evaluation skills, a phenomenon linked to "metacognitive laziness." title: Examining the Change in Social Studies Teacher Candidates’ Perceptions Regarding the Use of Film in Social Studies
text_snippet: Examining the Change in Social Studies Teacher Candidates’ Perceptions Regarding the Use of Film in Social Studies The purpose of this study is to examine the perceptions of social studies teacher candidates regarding the use of films in social studies. Through the analysis of human rights-based films, current approaches in social studies such as war, immigration, children's rights, refugee children's rights, women's rights, refugee women's rights, racism, artificial intelligence and ethics, justice, social justice, legal literacy, and political literacy were discussed. Six films were used during the 6-week research. The research sample, which was conducted using mixed methods, consists of 24 fourth-grade students studying in the Social Studies Education Department of Ege University. The perception scale for film usage, which is one of the quantitative data collection tools, was applied as a pretest and posttest. Data were analyzed with the T test (paired samples T test) for dependent groups in SPSS. Qualitative data collection tools including pre- and post-perception forms (2N) and interviews, were analyzed descriptively. Pre- and post-perception forms were analyzed using rubrics. title: The Effectiveness of Project-Based Learning Approach in Early Literacy Development
text_snippet: The Effectiveness of Project-Based Learning Approach in Early Literacy Development This research aims to investigate how the Project-Based Learning (PBL) method influences early literacy development in children aged 61-72 months attending preschool institutions. The study employs a quasi-experimental approach, utilizing pre-test and post-test control groups to determine whether PBL can improve essential literacy including receptive and expressive language, phonological awareness, letter knowledge, vocabulary, and writing awareness. The research involved 36 children, with 19 placed in the experimental group, where the PBL approach was implemented, and 17 assigned to the control group, which adhered to the standard preschool education curriculum. The data collection instrument utilized was the Reading and Writing Skills Research Test for 61-72 Month-Old Children (RWSRT). Data analysis was performed using SPSS 22.0, employing both independent samples t-tests and paired samples t-tests to evaluate and compare the pre-test and post-test outcomes for the experimental and control groups.Additionally, ANCOVA was applied to adjust for pre-test scores and evaluate the effect of the intervention. title: Adaptation of the Multicultural Sensitivity Scale for Pre-service Teachers into Turkish: Validation and Reliability Study
text_snippet: Adaptation of the Multicultural Sensitivity Scale for Pre-service Teachers into Turkish: Validation and Reliability Study In this study, the Multicultural Sensitivity Scale was adapted to Turkish culture by examining its psychometric properties among pre-service teachers. The research was conducted with data obtained from 610 pre-service teachers, 81 of which were used for linguistic equivalence, 392 for CFA and reliability analysis, and 137 for criterion validity. Firstly, the scale items were translated into Turkish by experts and back-translated. They were sent to the scale developers, and adjustments were made based on the feedback. In order to statistically determine the linguistic equivalence of the scale, the relationship between the original form and the Turkish form was examined and high relationships were found between the dimensions and total scores. In order to determine the construct validity of the Turkish form, the factor loadings and fit indices were examined as a result of the second order CFA. According to the CFA results, it was seen that the two-dimensional structure of the scale was preserved and the fit indices were at an acceptable level. title: Evaluation of the Teaching for Understanding Approach Based on Teacher Opinions
text_snippet: Evaluation of the Teaching for Understanding Approach Based on Teacher Opinions The purpose of this study is to evaluate the advantages, limitations, effectiveness, and challenges of the Teaching for Understanding approach based on teachers' opinions. To this end, ten teachers were first provided with a 9-week training program on this approach. During the training process, teachers were provided with theoretical information about the approach and were given the opportunity to prepare their own lesson plans based on this approach and implement them in their classrooms. Subsequently, an interview form was developed and the teachers who participated in the training were asked for their opinions on the approach. The data obtained from the interviews were loaded into the MaxQda 24 analysis program in pdf format and coded. The analysis file was reviewed again after a certain period of time, and the codes were finalized. The resulting coding system and direct quotations were presented to the reader in an objective manner. Based on the findings of the study, it was concluded that the Teaching for Understanding approach, which is considered effective, has many advantages, but also certain difficulties and limitations.

title: Mapping the Landscape of Micro Learning Research in Education: A Bibliometric Review
text_snippet: Mapping the Landscape of Micro Learning Research in Education: A Bibliometric Review The aim of this study is to determine trends, development trajectories, and structural features in the field by studying the academic publications on micro learning through bibliometric mapping methods. Within the scope of this study, a total of 139 publications that were reviewed in the Web of Science Core Collection between 2015-2025 through the keyword “micro learning” and that were found in the categories of “Educational Research” and “Education Scientific Disciplines” were analyzed. The analysis was carried out through a multi-stage bibliometric mapping process, including data extraction, data cleaning and standardization, network construction, and visualization of relationships across different bibliometric dimensions. In this study, bibliometric data such as co-authorship-countries, co-occurrence-author keyword, citation-documents, bibliographic coupling-documents, bibliographic coupling-organizations, and co-citation – cited authors were mapped. The findings show that publications on micro learning intensified between 2016-2020 but have shown a relative decline in recent years. title: The Examination of the Relationship Between Internet Addiction and Loneliness and Happiness in Middle School Students
text_snippet: The Examination of the Relationship Between Internet Addiction and Loneliness and Happiness in Middle School Students This study aims to investigate the relationship between internet addiction, loneliness, and school-related happiness among middle school students. This quantitative research was designed according to the correlational survey method. The research sample consists of 927 students attending various middle schools in the central district of Adıyaman province. Data were collected using the Personal Information Form, the Internet Addiction Scale, the Child-Centered Loneliness Scale for Grades 5-8, and the School Children’s Happiness Inventory. The findings revealed a moderately significant positive correlation between students’ levels of internet addiction and loneliness, as well as a moderately significant negative correlation between internet addiction and school happiness. Furthermore, both loneliness and happiness at school were found to be significant predictors of internet addiction. The results suggest that experiences of loneliness and reduced happiness at school may contribute to increased internet addiction among middle school students.

title: Adding New Skill in Backpack: Examining Teacher Candidates’ Experiences with AI-Supported Presentation Design
text_snippet: Adding New Skill in Backpack: Examining Teacher Candidates’ Experiences with AI-Supported Presentation Design The quality of presentation materials within the teaching through presentation approach, which has been widely used in teaching for many years, has been significantly transformed by the rapid development of artificial intelligence technologies and their integration into education. AI-supported presentations, enriched in terms of content production and visual design, enable the creation of learning environments that are sensitive to individual differences. Therefore, developing the skills of future teachers to effectively use artificial intelligence for pedagogical purposes in educational material development processes and integrating it into educational processes is critically important for increasing classroom interaction and diversifying teaching methods. Therefore, this research examines the experiences of 22 teacher candidates in their third year of undergraduate studies in social studies teacher education at a state university in preparing effective presentations using AI-supported presentation tools through collaborative pair work, using a mixed methods research approach. title: Preschool Teachers' Awareness of Climate Change: Educational Considerations to Global Issues
text_snippet: Preschool Teachers' Awareness of Climate Change: Educational Considerations to Global Issues Climate change is a significant global issue affecting many areas of life, and how this topic is addressed in early childhood is closely related to teachers' awareness and practices. This research is a qualitative study conducted to examine preschool teachers' awareness of climate change and how they reflect this awareness in their classroom practices. Twenty-one preschool teachers participated in the study, and data were collected through semi-structured interviews. The findings show that teachers mostly understand climate change in terms of global problems and observable environmental effects, while focusing on human-induced behaviors and industrialization in their explanations of the causes. Teachers' individual measures are mostly limited to daily practices such as recycling and energy conservation; participation in voluntary and collective environmental activities is low. The vast majority of teachers consider themselves partially adequate in raising children's awareness of climate change and express difficulties, particularly in concretizing abstract concepts, ensuring family participation, and instilling conscious consumption habits. title: The University Affected by the Business Sickness: A Performance Story
text_snippet: The University Affected by the Business Sickness: A Performance Story This study explores the opinions and experiences of academics regarding performance measurement and related processes implemented in universities in Turkey. A qualitative research design was employed. An open-ended questionnaire was administered via email to 34 academics working at nine different public universities, and the data were analyzed using content analysis. The findings reveal that a significant number of academics hold positive views of performance measurement. According to these academics, performance measurement enhances professional accountability, ensures objective evaluation, increases motivation, and promotes quality in academia. Paradoxically, the study also shows that many academics believe performance measurement has destructive effects on academic processes. They argue that performance measurement reshapes the traditional meaning, values, and practices of academia by imposing a competitive, business-oriented mindset. It reduces academic work to quantitative data, thereby subordinating quality. As a result, it generates conflicts in institutional culture and transformations in academic identity. title: Examining the Relationships Between Media Literacy Social Media Usage Habits and Motivation Among University Students
text_snippet: Examining the Relationships Between Media Literacy Social Media Usage Habits and Motivation Among University Students The aim of this research is to examine the predictive role of university students' new media literacy levels on their social media usage habits and motivations. The "New Media Literacy Scale" and "Social Media Usage Habits and Motivations Scale" were used as a data collection tool in this research. The data was obtained from 418 students studying in different faculties at Burdur Mehmet Akif Ersoy University. Multiple linear hierarchical regression analyses were applied to the analysis of the data. The study showed that the students' new media literacy levels were generally high, and that they mostly used social media for leisure time, social interaction, and information. Furthermore, a weakly significant positive correlation was found between new media literacy and social media usage habits and motivations. In the regression analysis, the functional prosumption sub-factor was found to be a significant predictor of social media usage motivations. The results reveal that media literacy is an important variable that determines how and for what purposes university students use social media.

title: Turkish Pre-service EFL Teachers’ Attitudes towards the Integration of the EPOSTL into Teacher Training Programs
text_snippet: Turkish Pre-service EFL Teachers’ Attitudes towards the Integration of the EPOSTL into Teacher Training Programs Self-assessment plays a key role in foreign language teacher education in terms of enhancing pre-service EFL teachers’ professional development. The European Portfolio of Student Teachers of Languages (EPOSTL) is a way of sustaining self-assessment practices among pre-service EFL teachers during their practicum period. Although the use of the EPOSTL is quite prevalent in global context, it is not commonly implemented in FLTE programs in the Turkish tertiary context. Due to the fact that the EPOSTL can have a rich potential to foster teaching competences of pre-service EFL teachers, it is important to investigate pre-service EFL teachers’ attitudes towards using this portfolio in their undergraduate programs. In this vein, the ultimate aim of this study is to explore pre-service EFL teachers’ general point of views regarding the use of the EPOSTL as a self-assessment tool in their undergraduate program. The study adopts a qualitative design based on a thematic analysis. The participants of the study are 31 senior year pre-service EFL teachers. title: Perspectives of Rural Primary School Students on the Concept of Artificial Intelligence
text_snippet: Perspectives of Rural Primary School Students on the Concept of Artificial Intelligence The popularity of artificial intelligence (AI), which represents the latest outcome of technological advancement, is increasing day by day. Various scenarios are being written about the possible future of AI. As artificial intelligence is sometimes regarded by people as a savior and at other times as a major threat, the opinions of children—who will become the adults of the future—are of great importance. The main purpose of this study is to reveal the metaphorical perceptions of primary school students living in rural areas toward the concept of artificial intelligence and to examine their thoughts on this concept in depth. In this research, the phenomenology design, one of the qualitative research methods, and the convenience sampling method, one of the purposive sampling techniques, were used. The study group consisted of 71 students studying at a primary school located in a rural neighborhood of the Terme district in Samsun. A semi-structured interview form was used as the data collection tool. title: Exploring the Mathematical Modeling Skills of Pre-Service Elementary Mathematics Teachers Through an Artificial Intelligence Tool: The Case of ChatGPT
text_snippet: Exploring the Mathematical Modeling Skills of Pre-Service Elementary Mathematics Teachers Through an Artificial Intelligence Tool: The Case of ChatGPT The aim of this study is to examine the mathematical modeling (MM) skills of pre-service elementary mathematics teachers (PEMTs) in the context of their interactions with ChatGPT, artificial intelligence (AI)-supported language model, and to analyze the process in a multifaceted and in-depth manner. A case study design, one of the qualitative research paradigms, was employed in the study. A total of 41 PEMTs participated in the study, and the participants were selected using criterion sampling, one of the purposive sampling methods. Data were collected through modeling tasks, AI interaction records, semi-structured interview forms, and observation notes. The collected data were analyzed using the content analysis method. The findings revealed that the MM competencies of the candidates varied depending on the difficulty level of the tasks. While receiving support from AI, the PEMTs mostly engaged in interactions such as explanatory and directive guidance, confirmatory feedback, strategy generation, and reflective questioning. title: An Inquiry through English Language Learning Experiences of Diverse Learners in a Public Education Setting
text_snippet: An Inquiry through English Language Learning Experiences of Diverse Learners in a Public Education Setting This study aims to investigate the English language learning experiences of students enrolled in the English course at a Public Education Center. Through this investigation, the study also aims to elicit students' prior English language learning experiences and explore factors that positively or negatively affected their knowledge of and attitudes toward English. The study employed a phenomenological qualitative design and collected data through students' written accounts (n=16) and individual interviews (n=10). Data were subjected to content analysis methods and excerpts were utilized to demonstrate the participants' views regarding their experiences. While data obtained from written accounts revealed the main themes of "student-related factors facilitating learning", "teacher-related factors facilitating learning", "unrealized opportunities for English improvement", and "regrets about unfulfilled potential", data obtained from the interviews included the themes of "motivation for being enrolled in an English course" "previous English learning experiences", "current English-learning experience", and "study habits facilitating learning". title: Human Rights Education in Curricula and Textbooks in Türkiye: From Generation of Rights to Intergenerational Justice
text_snippet: Human Rights Education in Curricula and Textbooks in Türkiye: From Generation of Rights to Intergenerational Justice This study investigates the way human rights education is covered in Social Studies and Civics lesson curricula and textbooks in Türkiye. The investigation included the analyses of 2018 Human Rights, Citizenship and Democracy Curriculum; Human Rights and Civics Education Curriculum as updated in 2024 and textbooks published by the Ministry of National Education. The main purpose of the study is to depict how the learning outputs in the curricula and textbooks are represented within the framework of generations of human rights.The research that was conducted through the document analysis method evaluated the way learning outcomes were handled in the curricula and textbooks within the context of first-generation rights, second-generation rights, third-generation rights, and fourth-generation rights. The findings indicated that, in the 2018 curriculum, classical right categories were emphasized more whereas, in the 2024 curriculum, third-generation rights, such as environment, peace, and solidarity were more prominent. title: General Education Teachers' Attitudes and Social Acceptance of Students with Special Needs in Inclusive Schools
text_snippet: General Education Teachers' Attitudes and Social Acceptance of Students with Special Needs in Inclusive Schools This study examines the attitudes and social acceptance (SA) of teachers from various disciplines working in general education schools that implement inclusive education. We employed a descriptive survey design within a quantitative framework. The sample comprised 201 teachers from different subject areas in primary and secondary schools under the Ministry of National Education (MoNE) where inclusive practices are implemented. We collected demographic data using a participant information form and obtained research data through two instruments: The Teachers' Attitudes Toward Students with Special Needs Scale and the Teacher Social Acceptance Scale for Individuals with Special Needs. We analyzed the data using SPSS software and interpreted the findings in light of existing literature. The results show that primary school teachers exhibit higher levels of SA and more positive attitudes toward students with special needs compared to secondary school teachers. Furthermore, teachers' attitudes and levels of SA vary by subject area. title: Validation of the Turkish Version of the 12-Item Aggression Questionnaire
text_snippet: Validation of the Turkish Version of the 12-Item Aggression Questionnaire The purpose of this study was to examine the validity and the reliability of the Turkish Version of the 12-Item Aggression Questionnaire (AQ-12). A total of 286 undergraduate students (217 female, 64 male) voluntarily participated in the study. Based on participants’ responses, statistical analyses were performed to assess the reliability, factor structure and validity of the Turkish Version of the AQ-12. Reliability analysis of the scale revealed good internal consistency (Cronbach’s α = .84), and confirmatory factor analysis supported its single-factor structure. Moreover, convergent validity of the scale was confirmed by the significant positive correlation with the Revised Cyber Bullying Inventory for University Students (RCBI)(r = .37, p .05). The findings revealed that the Turkish Version of the AQ-12 is a valid and reliable tool for measuring aggression among university students. title: Investigating the Relationship Between Technology-Related Variables and Middle School Students’ Self-Regulation and Self-Directed Learning with Technology
text_snippet: Investigating the Relationship Between Technology-Related Variables and Middle School Students’ Self-Regulation and Self-Directed Learning with Technology Self-regulation and self-directedness have recently become closely associated with technology. The aim of this study is to examine middle school students’ levels of self-regulation skills and self-directed learning (SDL) with technology in terms of technology-related variables. The study was conducted using the general survey model, and the participant group consisted of 468 middle school students. The study revealed that middle school students' self-regulation skills and their levels of SDL with technology significantly varied based on how frequently they used e-learning platforms outside of school, in favor of those who used them more frequently. It was also determined that students' self-regulation skills and their SDL with technology significantly differed based on their purpose of technology use, and students who used technology for educational purposes had significantly higher self-regulation skills and SDL with technology compared to those who used it primarily for communication or entertainment. title: The Impact of 7E Learning Model Based Social Studies Education on Students’ Entrepreneurship Level
text_snippet: The Impact of 7E Learning Model Based Social Studies Education on Students’ Entrepreneurship Level Entrepreneurship is one of the common skills that the social studies course and the 7E learning model purpose to provide students with. The main purpose of this study is to determine the impact of 7E learning model based social studies education on students' entrepreneurship level. The participant group, which was conducted with an embedded design from mixed research methods, consisted of 5th grade students studying in a public secondary school in Ağrı province of Türkiye and the social studies teacher of these students. The data of the study were collected using the Entrepreneurship Scale for Secondary School Students, semi structured interview forms and unstructured observation form. In the study independent samples t-test and covariance analysis were utilized during analysis of the statistical data, and content analysis was used to analyze the qualitative data. In the study, it was concluded that 7E learning model based social studies education increased the level of entrepreneurship skill of secondary school students. title: The Use of Taxonomies in Constructing Text-Based Reading Comprehension Questions: Bloom and Barrett Taxonomies
text_snippet: The Use of Taxonomies in Constructing Text-Based Reading Comprehension Questions: Bloom and Barrett Taxonomies The aim of this study is to investigate how preservice Turkish language teachers construct reading comprehension questions based on Bloom’s and Barrett’s taxonomies. Adopting a qualitative case study design, data were collected through interviews, observations, and document analysis. The study focuses on the cognitive levels of the questions, participants’ perceptions and preferences regarding the taxonomies, reported changes in pedagogical awareness and professional competence following taxonomy-based instruction, and the challenges encountered during the question-design process. The findings suggest that preservice teachers tended to engage more with higher-order cognitive processes when using Barrett’s taxonomy during the question-design process. Participants perceived Barrett’s taxonomy as more functional and structured for evaluating reading comprehension, particularly in relation to inferential, evaluative, and affective aspects. In contrast, Bloom’s taxonomy was more commonly associated with questions targeting lower- and mid-level cognitive skills, such as remembering and understanding, whereas higher-level categories were addressed less frequently. title: Establishing Standards for Learner-Centered Education in Higher Education: A Comprehensive Framework for Türkiye
text_snippet: Establishing Standards for Learner-Centered Education in Higher Education: A Comprehensive Framework for Türkiye This study explored the key standards and sub-standards for constructing learner-centered education in higher education in Türkiye. Using a qualitative multimethod design, data were collected through individual interviews, focus group discussions, and document analysis. Participants included 12 administrators (7 male, 5 female) and 12 faculty members (4 male, 8 female) from accredited science and social science programs at six public and six private universities in Ankara. Focus group interviews involved 101 third- and fourth-year students across 12 groups from the same institutions. Document analysis encompassed 57 national and international sources, including articles, books, project reports, quality assurance standards, and policy documents, dated between 1979 and 2023. Interviews were conducted from September 2021 to February 2022, while document analysis occurred from February 2021 to June 2023. Inductive data analysis involved coding, identifying patterns, and developing categories and themes. title: Comparing Creativity in Early Childhood Curricula: New Zealand and Finland
text_snippet: Comparing Creativity in Early Childhood Curricula: New Zealand and Finland Early childhood is of critical importance for creativity, and creativity is among the 21st-century skills. The research aims to investigate the inclusion of creativity within the national early childhood curricula of New Zealand and Finland and to compare these curricula. The research is qualitative, and the document analysis method was used. The study group consists of the early childhood curricula of New Zealand and Finland. The findings indicate that creativity is embedded in both curricula through three overarching dimensions: program, child, and teacher. The research concluded that both curricula were flexible and acknowledged play as a powerful means of expressing creativity. Both curricula recognized children as individuals capable of thinking and acting creatively, emphasizing the diversity of materials and learning experiences to foster creativity. It was concluded that teachers in both curricula have similar roles and responsibilities in supporting and developing creativity, acting as key facilitators who design responsive and stimulating learning settings. title: Climate Change Education in Context: A Comparative Analysis of Secondary-School Level Policies, Pedagogies, and Practices in Türkiye and Sweden
text_snippet: Climate Change Education in Context: A Comparative Analysis of Secondary-School Level Policies, Pedagogies, and Practices in Türkiye and Sweden This study offers a comparative analysis of climate change education (CCE) in secondary education in Türkiye and Sweden, examining how national contexts shape the curricular integration, pedagogical approaches, technological tools, and teacher preparation related to climate education. Drawing on a qualitative document analysis of national curricula, policy frameworks, and official support materials, and guided by Bray and Thomas’s multilevel comparative framework as well as Crossley and Watson’s emphasis on contextual sensitivity, the research highlights how governance structures, historical legacies, and educational traditions influence the design and delivery of CCE. Sweden emerges as a case of systemic and participatory integration of CCE, supported by interdisciplinary curricula, experiential learning methods, and sustained teacher development. In contrast, Türkiye’s approach reflects centralized policy-making, fragmented curricular implementation, and limited pedagogical support, despite recent advances such as the Environmental Education and Climate Change course. title: EFL Teachers’ (Generation X and Y) and Learners’ (Generation Z) Perceptions On 21st Century Skills
text_snippet: EFL Teachers’ (Generation X and Y) and Learners’ (Generation Z) Perceptions On 21st Century Skills This quantitative study intended to reveal the perceptions of Generation X and Generation Y EFL teachers and learners of Generation Z regarding their competency of and the importance they attach to the 21st century skills. The results of the study indicated that Gen Xers deem themselves very competent whereas Gen Ys and Gen Zs view themselves as moderately competent in terms of the 21st century skills. Also, the Generation X esteem 21st century skills the most important among the whole group. The findings suggest that, regardless of their generation, the EFL teachers should be aware of and equipped with 21st century skills to assist learners from different generations. Besides, the needs of Gen Zs and the curriculum should be reviewed meticulously so that the members of this generation might perceive themselves more competent learners. Thus, EFL teachers should be knowledgeable about the importance of 21st century skills and the generational differences throughout their education. Therefore, Gen Z can obtain utmost benefit from the Gen X and Gen Y EFL instructors. title: Assessment of Early Mathematics Skills of Preschool Children According to Socioeco-nomic Status
text_snippet: Assessment of Early Mathematics Skills of Preschool Children According to Socioeco-nomic Status This study aims to evaluate the early mathematics skills of children aged 60 to 72 months attend-ing kindergartens in Ankara and to develop a skill profile based on the assessment results. A total of 300 children (152 girls and 148 boys) from various socioeconomic backgrounds, en-rolled in either independent kindergartens or preschool classes within primary schools affiliated with the Ministry of National Education, were included in the study. The children's mathematical skills were assessed using the Early Mathematics Skills Assessment Tool (MATBED), which was specifically developed for preschool children and validated through reliability and validity stud-ies. MATBED consists of five subtests: Digit Recognition, Addition-Subtraction, Grouping, Pat-tern, and Geometry. The collected data were analyzed in SPSS in two stages. In the first stage, descriptive statistics of the scores obtained from MATBED were presented, and the distribution of results across each subtest was examined. In the second stage, the study explored whether early mathematics skills varied according to socioeconomic status. title: Identifying the Expectations and Suggestions of Parents of Students with Specific Learning Difficulties Regarding Special Education and Rehabilitation Centers
text_snippet: Identifying the Expectations and Suggestions of Parents of Students with Specific Learning Difficulties Regarding Special Education and Rehabilitation Centers This study aims to identify the expectations and suggestions of parents of children with specific learning difficulties (SLD) regarding special education and rehabilitation centers. SLD is a condition where individuals face neurodevelopmental challenges in acquiring and utilizing skills in areas such as speech, reading, writing, and mathematics. The study focuses on parents' lack of knowledge during the diagnosis process and their expectations from educational centers. The research was conducted using the phenomenology method, one of the qualitative research designs. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with ten parents whose children with SLD have been receiving special education services for at least six months. The data were analyzed by creating themes, and participants were selected using purposive and snowball sampling techniques. title: An Evaluation of Institutions Assigning Teachers for Teaching Turkish Abroad and Their Teacher Selection Processes
text_snippet: An Evaluation of Institutions Assigning Teachers for Teaching Turkish Abroad and Their Teacher Selection Processes Turkey assigns teachers/academics abroad to help Turks living overseas learn their native language and stay connected to Turkish culture and to enable foreigners to learn Turkish and become acquainted with Turkish culture. As a result, Turkish can now be taught face-to-face in more than a hundred countries. This study investigated which institutions assign teachers abroad and how the assignment process works. Within the scope of the research, variables such as the teacher selection method, required qualifications, duration of the assignment, and the scope of duties during the process from application to departure abroad were examined. The study, conducted as qualitative research, gathered its data through document analysis. For this purpose, published guidelines and announcements on the institutions’ official websites were treated and examined as documents. In the analyses, a scenario was developed to highlight the similarities and differences between the institutions. The evaluation found that the Ministry of National Education of the Republic of Turkey, the Yunus Emre Institute, and the Turkish Maarif Foundation assign teachers or academics abroad. title: Investigation of the Relationship Between Peer Bullying and School-Based Loneliness in Primary School Children
text_snippet: Investigation of the Relationship Between Peer Bullying and School-Based Loneliness in Primary School Children This study aimed to investigate the relationship between peer bullying and school-based loneliness in primary school children. Designed as a descriptive and cross-sectional study, it was conducted with the participation of 453 third- and fourth-grade primary school students enrolled in a school located in a province in the Southeastern Region of Turkey. Data were collected using the Demographic Information Form, the Peer Bullying Scale - Child Form, and the School-Based Loneliness Scale. Statistical analyses included frequency, percentage, arithmetic mean, standard deviation, t-test, ANOVA, Mann–Whitney U test, Kruskal–Wallis test, and Spearman correlation. The mean scores obtained were 22.83±25.19 for the Peer Bullying Scale - Victim Subscale, 8.67±15.20 for the Peer Bullying Scale - Bully Subscale, and 22.89±10.73 for the School-Based Loneliness Scale. The findings indicated a positive correlation between being a victim and being a perpetrator of peer bullying among primary school students. title: Non-Cognitive Entrepreneurship Competent Scale for Secondary School Students: A Validity and Reliability Study
text_snippet: Non-Cognitive Entrepreneurship Competent Scale for Secondary School Students: A Validity and Reliability Study The aim of this study is to develop a measurement tool to determine the non-cognitive entrepreneurial competents of secondary school students. The study group of the research consists of 562 students studying in a public secondary school in Kars province in the 2021-2022 academic year. First of all, the literature was examined in order to determine the non-cognitive entrepreneurship competents that can be acquired by secondary school students. A draft form consisting of items covering the determined competens was created. To ensure the content validity of the prepared form, six experts were evaluated. As a result of the feedback, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) and criterion-related validity studies were conducted for the construct validity of the finalized form. For exploratory factor analysis, the form was applied to 293 secondary school students and as a result of the factor analysis, it was determined that the scale consisted of 29 items and three dimensions, and it was aimed to verify the scale and dimensions with confirmatory factor analysis. title: Preschool Pre-service Teachers' Understanding of Human Internal Organs: An Investigation through the Lens of Mental Models
text_snippet: Preschool Pre-service Teachers' Understanding of Human Internal Organs: An Investigation through the Lens of Mental Models This study aimed to investigate preschool pre-service teachers’ mental models related to the internal organs of the human body. The research sample consisted of 141 preschool pre-service teachers enrolled in the 1st through 4th of a state university in Turkey. The participants were selected using a convenience sampling method. Two data collection instruments were used: an Interview Form and a Drawing Form. Given the use of both qualitative and quantitative data, a mixed-methods approach was adopted. Interpretive content analysis was employed to examine the qualitative data, while descriptive and inferential statistical techniques were applied to analyze the quantitative data. The findings revealed that most teacher candidates possessed adequate mental models of the internal organs, although some held misconceptions regarding their shapes, locations, and functions. While no significant differences were found in mental models based on gender, a notable variation was observed across grade levels.

title: A Scoping Review of Studies Focusing on Professionals Providing Services for Young Children with Disabilities During The COVID-19 Pandemic
text_snippet: A Scoping Review of Studies Focusing on Professionals Providing Services for Young Children with Disabilities During The COVID-19 Pandemic The pandemic transformed the service delivery by the professionals working with young children with disabilities as a result of the suspension of in-person services. This paper provides a scoping review of research articles carried out on the professionals providing services for young children with disabilities during the COVID-19 pandemic. It also synthetizes the findings of research articles on the topic to identify the gaps and trends in this knowledgebase in order to guide further research. The guidelines on the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses (PRISMA) were followed. The studies were analyzed considering the year of publication, source of the country, distribution of the articles across journals, participants, methodology used, focus and the findings of the studies. Results indicated that most of the studies have investigated the challenges that the professionals encountered during the remote services, and how they adapted to remotely delivering the services. Limitations, implications for research and practice were also discussed.

title: The Ghostwriter Paradox: Why we must move from AI Literacy to AI Fluency
text_snippet: The Ghostwriter Paradox: Why we must move from AI Literacy to AI Fluency For years, those of us in educational technology promised that digital tools would transform schools. Well, the transformation is finally here, but it did not arrive as a gentle evolution. It hit us like a shockwave. We are now facing what I call the "Ghostwriter Paradox". In the old days, a ghostwriter was a luxury, someone paid to write a book while another person took the credit. Today, Generative AI has become the world’s cheapest, most available ghostwriter. Here is the problem: When a student asks a chatbot to author an essay, the student’s name goes on the paper, but the actual thinking happens inside the machine. Writing isn't about putting words on a page; it is a struggle that forces us to organize our thoughts. When we outsource that struggle to an algorithm, students lose the chance to build their own mental structures. They risk becoming mentally lazy, acting as passive verifiers instead of active thinkers. So, what do we do? First, we need to stop talking about "AI Literacy" and start talking about "AI Fluency". title: The Effect of Technology-Supported 5E Model Practice on Academic Success in Equality and Equations
text_snippet: The Effect of Technology-Supported 5E Model Practice on Academic Success in Equality and Equations The aim of this study is to investigate the effect of technology-based implementation of the 5E model on students' academic achievement in the subject of equality and equivalence. The study group consisted of 64 students, 31 girls and 33 boys, studying in seventh grade in a public school in Karaman province, Turkey, in the 2021-2022 academic year. In the study, different education programs were applied to three different groups. The control group was taught the subject of equality and equations by applying the current curriculum. To measure the academic achievement of the students, the Equality and Equations Achievement Test was applied to all groups as a pre-test and post-test. The one-way ANOVA, Wilcoxon, and t-test were performed using a statistical program. text_snippet: An Investigation of the Relationship Between State Anxiety and Emotional Intelligence Levels of 8th Grade Students This study aims to examine the relationship between state anxiety and emotional intelligence levels of 8th-grade students who simultaneously experience adolescence and the high school entrance exam. title: Integrating STEM into Mathematics Teacher Candidate Education: Experiences, Challenges, and Reflections
text_snippet: Integrating STEM into Mathematics Teacher Candidate Education: Experiences, Challenges, and Reflections The integration of STEM education into mathematics teacher preparation programs has become increasingly vital to equip future educators with interdisciplinary skills required for 21st century learning environments. Considering this situation, this study explores the experiences, challenges, and reflections of mathematics teacher candidates during a STEM-based activity which was designed within the scope of teacher education. In this direction, a case study was conducted with 19 mathematics teacher candidates from a state university in Türkiye. Data were collected through a Product Evaluation Rubric, Product Evaluation Form, and an Opinion Form developed by the researchers. Obtained data was analyzed by means of qualitative approaches. The findings revealed that although all participants were conceptually familiar with STEM, they lacked prior experience in a practical STEM activity. title: Measuring Students' Instantaneous Attention Levels in Classroom Environment: Development and Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence Software
text_snippet: Measuring Students' Instantaneous Attention Levels in Classroom Environment: Development and Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence Software This study aimed to develop and implement an artificial intelligence (AI) software to measure students' attention levels in real-time during class. Additionally, the research explored instructors' perspectives on the use of AI for monitoring attention in the classroom. The quantitative phase of the research was conducted during the fall semester of 2021-2022 with 396 students from the Forensic Informatics Department at Fırat University. The qualitative phase involved five instructors participating in the software application. In the quantitative phase, data were collected using the AI software, an attention control scale, and an attention labeling form completed by three experts. A semi-structured interview form was used for the qualitative phase. The AI algorithm was developed by utilizing publicly available online photos to classify students' attention levels.
